== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns Margaret Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Margrat Glasgow and John Aiton on 18 October 1693 at Cambusnethan.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 628/10 / 344; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Margaret Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Margaret Glasgow and John Tailzer on 18 December 1690 at Walston.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 658/10 / 206; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Margaret Glasgow. Betham’s abstract of Archibald Glasgow of Rathmalton, clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, names his wife Elizabeth, Thomas Glasgow as eldest son and Margaret as only daughter. Margaret’s husband is an unnamed Cairns, and Thomas Cairns is her son.<ref>Archibald Glasgow’s will abstract names his eldest son Thomas; [https://catalogue.nli.ie/Record/vtls000540633 record].</ref> Betham’s pre-destruction derivative abstract was inspected, not the original will. The father–son statement is explicit; identification of the son with [[Glasgow-3556]] remains strongly probable, with no residence or estate bridge. Elizabeth’s surname remains provisional. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Margaret Glasgow in Byris, Kilwinning, 1636. The printed Glasgow testament index records “Margaret, in Byris of Kilwinning” on 8 November 1636. This may be [[Glasgow-1100]], who was baptised in 1610 and married by 1632, but the index gives no spouse, kin, occupation or link to Byris. The date is the index entry date, not a proved death date. Identity remains unresolved pending the underlying testament. The identification remains uncertain.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), printed p.196, Margaret in Byris of Kilwinning, 8 November 1636, Glasgow Commissary Court CC9/7/27; [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso07scotuoft.pdf#page=206 scanned printed index, PDF p.206]. The underlying testament has not been inspected.</ref>
